smells.finding: Longest function (fit_driver_fingerprints, ~55 lines) delegates to _read_observable_rows/_fit_channel/_aggregate_cells; the implementer already refactored _aggregate_cells after simplification_limits flagged cyclomatic_complexity=20 (split into _row_to_bucket_item/_optional_weighted_mean/_combine_bucket), and the tool re-passes.
Only one class in fit.py: _CellAggregate, a 4-field frozen dataclass (data holder, not a large class).

test_g_sigma_onesided_changes_sigma_not_mean and test_nonzero_lapsampling_widens_sigma repeat the identical 5-step arrange/act/assert shape (build two DBs with an override, two stores, fit both, assert mean equal + sigma greater) almost verbatim. A shared helper (e.g. _fit_two_scenarios_and_assert_sigma_widens) would remove the duplication. Minor -- readability of an independent test case arguably outweighs the extraction here -- observation, not a blocker.
_price_sigma_with_shared_floor delegates the actual quadrature math to pool_random_effects rather than reaching into its internals; no method operates mostly on another object's data.

_row_to_bucket_item/_combine_bucket thread an anonymous 5-tuple (weight, value, n_eff_contribution, g_sigma_onesided, sigma_lapsampling) through four positional-unpack sites in _combine_bucket (`for w, _v, _n, _g, _s in items` repeated 4x with different fields selected). A small named NamedTuple/dataclass for the per-row contribution would remove the positional-index fragility. Minor/non-blocking -- the tuple never crosses the module boundary and simplification_limits already passes.

Same root cause as the data-clumps finding above: the per-row contribution is a bare tuple rather than a small typed structure. Grouped with the data-clumps finding (one underlying cause), not double-counted as a separate blocker.

fit_driver_fingerprints takes 3 positional + 9 keyword-only params (12 total). It scales up store.write_fingerprint's own existing convention (6 positional + 1 kwarg) to also cover DB-read config (season/session_type/map_version/as_of_round/channels). Worth a future params-object refactor if the signature grows further, but it matches the package's existing explicit-kwarg style (CREW_CONTEXT: match surrounding conventions) and every param is independently meaningful with sensible defaults -- non-blocking observation.
Single new module, single call site into store.write_fingerprint; no ripple across other files required for this change.
fit.py has one reason to change (the G3 fit hierarchy); it does not mix unrelated concerns (no I/O formatting, no CLI, no unrelated schema logic).
No multi-hop attribute chains in fit.py; deepest access is a single .get() or .predict() call on a locally-held object.

The `channels` parameter (default FINGERPRINT_CHANNELS) is exercised by TestBothChannelsWritten and gives a real, currently-useful partial-refit hook; no unused hooks, abstract base classes, or dead extension points were added.

Docstrings are precise and tied to concrete invariants/tests/decision docs (e.g. citing #628's 14.6x precedent, the exact test class names) -- they explain intent behind already-clear code, not covering up confusion.
